editor_notes.factual_accuracy: One misattribution found. The article's closing 'What We Know' bullet states the Skullcandy-Bose partnership 'unveiled at a New York event in April 2025 that Skullcandy "brand ambassador and sound lab consultant Tony Hawk was in attendance" for.' Checking the raw HTML of the Popular Science source (source-2), that exact sentence is a <figcaption> attached to a photo from the July 15, 2026 Crusher 1080 ANC launch event (the subject of this very article) -- not a description of the April 2025 Method 360 ANC unveiling. The full caption also reads 'Tony Hawk was in attendance, in spirit and likeness,' meaning he was represented symbolically/in imagery rather than confirmed to be physically present, a qualifier the article drops. Popular Science's article body does not state whether Tony Hawk personally attended the April 2025 event. This is a single, subordinate specific in the body (not in the headline, summary, or Overview lead) and is honestly correctable with a public corrections note. All other claims, quotes, and figures across all 7 sources checked out with no other discrepancies.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout. No editorializing or sensationalism from the bot itself. The automated 'loaded language' (clearly) and 'sensationalist language' (incredible) flags are false positives -- both instances are verbatim direct quotes from a Techlicious reviewer and from CEO Garofalow's press-release quote, correctly set off in quotation marks and attributed, not the bot's own framing.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. Searched src/content/articles/2026-07/ and 2026-06/ for 'skullcandy', 'crusher 1080', and 'bose' -- no overlap with any previously published article.
concerns: Misattributed quote: the 'Tony Hawk was in attendance' detail is sourced from a Popular Science photo caption describing the July 15, 2026 launch event, not the April 2025 partnership-unveiling event as the article implies, and the article drops the caption's 'in spirit and likeness' qualifier that indicates symbolic rather than confirmed physical attendance. Filing a corrections record.
